newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH COALITION DEPUTIES TO MEET ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH COALITION DEPUTIES TO MEET ON TUESDAY.

text.p: Caucusses of the Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Polish Peasant Party will hold a rare meeting on Tuesday to discuss the future of their ruling coalition amid a row over a planned cabinet reshuffle.

The parliamentary press office said on Monday that the joint meeting, one of just a handful since the two parties formed their unesay coalition in 1993, was scheduled for Tuesday afternoon outside parliament's premises.

The Peasant party demanded that the crisis meeting be held nearly three weeks ago when its member, Jacek Buchacz, was abruptly ousted by SLD's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz over alleged irregularities in his ministry.
Buchacz dismissal aggravated a dispute between the two parties over a cabinet reshuffle, which will accompany a coming reorganisation of ministries.
The quarrel concerns mainly appointments in three crucial economic ministries of economy, treasury and finance as well as a method of tranforming the current cabinet into a new one.
The SLD wants ministers to be replaced gradually since October, when the cabinet reform is launched with the creation of the treasury ministry.
The Peasant party says the whole current cabinet should be dismissed in a parliamentary vote and a new one promptly formed.

Analysts say the first method will give a decisive say on the line-up of the new cabinet to Prime Minister Cimoszewicz and President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who are linked to the SLD. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
